hook: A cage molecule binds iodide in water as strongly as biological binders, excluding other halides.
summary: Chemists built an organic cage with halogen- and hydrogen-bond donors. Its halogen-bonding pocket picks out iodide in water with a binding constant of 43,000 per molar, and in DMSO/water it holds iodide plus chloride at once. Results are from NMR titrations of one cage design, not tests in real water samples.
title: Simultaneous Selective Recognition of Two Different Anions within a Hydrogen/Halogen-Bonding Cage
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
